Senses.Explanation: Without marks, or markless, is a phrase for being apart from marks, appearance, or form. It is attested within 2,588 total occurrences across 324 allowlisted texts. Huineng's Platform Record gives a direct definition: "markless means being among marks while apart from marks" (無相者，於相而離相). It also says the teaching establishes "marklessness as its body" (無相為體, 11 occurrences). A later small assembly quotes that three-part formula and asks why marklessness is not also made the source. In a Compendium encounter, an unnamed questioner asks, "what is without marks?" and Layman Pangyun answers, "mountains green, waters verdant" (如何是無相；山青水綠). Transmission wording places "true form, markless" (實相無相, 103) between "the subtle mind of extinction" and "subtle correct teaching." The corpus further records Mazu Daoyi asking how to accord with "markless complete command" (無相三昧). These definitions, questions, compounds, and quotations keep the phrase tied to marks and their absence; this entry does not turn it into an imported theory.
Senses.Note: The source text's two-graph term can be adjectival or nominal. The direct "among marks while apart from marks" definition occurs in two Platform Record witnesses. The homographic title-name Wuxiang is separated below.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Record of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經), spoken by Huineng. Huineng directly defines markless as being among marks while apart from marks.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是無相。師曰。山青水綠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Layman Pangyun section. An unnamed questioner is the exact speaker asking what is without marks; Layman Pangyun answers with green mountains and verdant waters. All six attribution rungs leave the questioner personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 吾以清淨法眼涅槃妙心實相無相微妙正法將付於汝
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄) quotes Shakyamuni Buddha's transmission statement. Shakyamuni Buddha is the exact speaker who places true form, markless within the entrusted teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 早叅舉六祖大師無相為體無念為本無住為宗師云既云無相為體何不即以無相為宗既云無念為本何不即以無念為宗
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of State Preceptor Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), in Yulin Tongxiu's morning address. Yulin explicitly raises Huineng's formulation 'marklessness as body, no-thought as basis, non-abiding as source' (無相為體，無念為本，無住為宗); Huineng is the exact quoted speaker. The headword inside the saying does not refer to Master Wuxiang.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂問。如何用心即合無相三昧。讓曰。汝學心地法門如下種子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄) recounts Mazu Daoyi's exchange with Nanyue Huairang. Mazu Daoyi is the exact speaker asking how to accord with markless complete command; Nanyue begins the answer with the field of mind and a seed.

Senses.Explanation: As a personal name, Wuxiang is the Yizhou master named in lineage headings. The Linked Lamps lists "one lineage heir of Master Wuxiang of Yizhou" (益州無相禪師法嗣一人), namely Wuzhu of Baotang in the following text. Two independent lamp histories likewise place Baotang Wuzhu under this heading and say that Wuzhu first received the teaching from Master Wuxiang (初得法於無相大師). These occurrences name a person and must not be translated as the adjective "markless."
Senses.Note: The full string "Wuxiang of Yizhou" (益州無相) occurs 17 times and "Master Wuxiang" (無相禪師) 18. Three curated witnesses establish the same Yizhou-master/Baotang-Wuzhu lineage relation; unrelated people who may also bear the name are not silently identified with him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州無相禪師法嗣一人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Lamps Essential Compendium (聯燈會要), lineage heading for Wuxiang. Wuxiang is the named master in the heading 'one lineage heir of Master Wuxiang of Yizhou.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州保唐寺無住禪師初得法於無相大師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Baotang Wuzhu section. Wuxiang is the named master from whom Baotang Wuzhu first received the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 益州保唐寺無住禪師。初得法於無相大師。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Baotang Wuzhu section. Wuxiang is the named master from whom Baotang Wuzhu first received the teaching.
